descriptionChirho: Masculine noun מִפְתָּן denoting a threshold or doorsill — the stone or timber at the base of a doorway that one steps over to enter a building, especially a temple or sacred space. Used of the threshold of the Philistine temple of Dagon (1 Sam 5:4,5), the threshold of the eschatological temple in Ezekiel's vision (Ezek 9:3, 10:4,18, 46:2, 47:1), and the threshold of the Jerusalem temple (Zeph 1:9). Multilingual evidence is consistent: eng threshold, spa umbral, hin दहलीज/देहली, arb عَتَبَة, kor 문지방, swa kizingiti. The construct ('threshold-of') and articled ('the-threshold') forms are grammatical variations, not semantic distinctions.
